Details: Scan a configurable root for .lattices.json, list configured projects, and show their panes and running session status.
Caveat: Discovery scans up to three levels and skips .git and node_modules.

Details: Detect Bun, pnpm, Yarn, or npm and select dev, start, serve, or watch from package.json.
Caveat: CLI and app have different package-manager precedence if multiple lockfiles exist.

Details: Identify each project session by its directory basename and six hexadecimal SHA-256 characters from the absolute path.
Caveat: Renaming or moving a project changes its session identity.

Details: Declare pane names, commands and first-pane width; build a two-pane split or a main pane with supporting panes.
Caveat: Requires tmux. With no detected dev command and no configured panes, the default is a single shell.

Details: Create or reconnect to a project session; launch, attach, detach, list or kill sessions through CLI and native controls.
Caveat: Requires tmux. Sessions survive terminal closure or disconnection; reboot survival is not implemented by ordinary tmux creation.

Details: On reattach, rerun exited commands automatically with ensure, or type them into idle panes for manual submission with prefill.
Caveat: Requires tmux and an idle pane recognized as a shell. Ensure takes precedence when both flags are enabled.

Details: Recreate missing panes, restore pane labels and restart declared commands in idle panes.
Caveat: Requires tmux. Layout is reapplied when missing panes are recreated; this is not a continuous background reconciler.

Details: Restart a pane command by name or index, first interrupting it and escalating if it remains running.
Caveat: Requires tmux. Restart can terminate child processes; a pane without a declared command is left at its shell.

Details: Launch work in Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, Kitty or Alacritty, choosing among installed terminals.
Caveat: Terminal and iTerm2 have specific focus/attach scripting; other terminals use app activation on this path.

Details: Detect Node, Swift, Rust, Go, Make or the Lattices hybrid project and run or build it with lats dev.
Caveat: The corresponding toolchain must be installed. Non-Lattices restart delegates to build rather than restarting an arbitrary service.

Details: Group terminal projects and application windows; match app titles, open missing URLs or apps, and select tabs by label or index.
Caveat: Configured groups persist in workspace.json; terminal project members require tmux.

Details: Create a group from selected existing windows, focus its members, split them side by side, collapse them or ungroup them.
Caveat: Live stacks are runtime-only. Hiding floating controls does not delete the group.

Details: Gather project and app windows into named layers; switch context, explicitly apply tiles, or launch missing members.
Caveat: Current configuration is ~/.lattices/workspace.json. Switching, tiling and launching are distinct operations.

Details: Match app names, titles and sessions with exact, substring or regular-expression criteria, plus Space, visibility and exclusions.
Caveat: Every field inside a clause must match. The retired ~/.lattices/layers.json file is no longer read.

Details: Add a window to a layer, pin it across title changes, remove eligible single-window entries, or move it between layers.
Caveat: A broad entry that also matches other windows can prevent removing only one member; edit the rule instead.

Details: Resolve each content window to at most one layer using pin, matching rule, group, project, then app/title precedence.
Caveat: Configured entries and live matching windows are separate states. Saved pins have explicit close/rebind semantics.

Details: Arrange layer windows with Auto, Columns or Master-stack; adapt Auto to standard and ultrawide displays.
Caveat: Automatic layout acts on the main display's current desktop. Explicit tile or display entries keep their assigned place.

Details: Hide unused apps, park other windows of shared apps, and restore a layer's additional scene windows when returning.
Caveat: Operates on the main display and current desktop. Some apps refuse off-screen parking; other displays and desktops stay in place.

Details: Restore parked frames and apps hidden by layer switches, including saved parking recovery after an app crash.
Caveat: Windows on another desktop may need that desktop to be shown before restoration. Apps hidden independently by the user stay hidden.

Details: Switch using eight direct slots around a 3×3 pad or directional arrows; use the center slot to show the current layer.
Caveat: Eight is the direct shortcut capacity, not a demonstrated hard maximum on saved layer count.

Details: Create, rename or delete layers; add, replace or remove entries; change layout while maintaining active-layer selection.
Caveat: Saved configuration changes take effect through the documented switch or explicit rearrangement actions.

Details: See scaled monitor maps and their desktops, with a tray for windows the maps cannot place and an on-demand working list.
Caveat: Current working-source implementation, including uncommitted changes; release and installed-app behavior were not reverified in this audit.

Details: Browse by layer, monitor, desktop, window kind or search, and select or extend a window selection without rearranging the desktop.
Caveat: Choosing a layer in Overview scopes inspection; it does not activate that layer.

Details: Distinguish live, last-known and saved-home positions, and show whether a window is visible, elsewhere, full screen, hidden, parked or unlocated.
Caveat: Unknown placement is labeled rather than invented. Saved configuration does not prove a currently open matching window.

Details: Focus or place one window, carry it to another desktop on its monitor, or tile, distribute and arrange a selected group per monitor.
Caveat: Only eligible windows are moved; excluded windows remain selected and untouched. Individual placement requires the monitor's current desktop.

Details: Edit a layer's layout and tucked windows, save configuration alone, or save and rearrange the active layer.
Caveat: Save and rearrange is offered only for the active layer; failed saving prevents rearrangement.

Details: Find windows, applications, configured projects, sessions, layers, groups and actions from a shared search surface.
Caveat: Search results depend on the available inventory. The default daemon search excludes OCR unless explicitly requested.

Details: Search titles, apps, sessions, working directories, terminal tabs, tmux metadata, processes and indexed OCR with explicit source selection.
Caveat: --deep and --all request every source. Terminal inspection and OCR availability depend on the relevant app support and permissions.

Details: Filter search by time and recency, return JSON or window IDs, and report matched sources and terminal details.
Caveat: Results refer to the observed inventory and can become stale before a later mutation.

Details: Draw a proportional terminal floor plan or versioned JSON projection, preserving monitor topology, window geometry and per-display front-to-back order.
Caveat: Current-Space windows only. Prefers desktop.snapshot and falls back on older builds; this opens no visible Lattices UI.

Details: Move one or several selected windows to the next or a named monitor while keeping normalized frames, or move and place one in a specific slot.
Caveat: Requires available display topology and Accessibility. Move-and-place is intentionally omitted for multi-selection to avoid stacking it into one slot.

Details: Focus a project's terminal across Spaces, using window tags and available native fallback paths, and switch adjacent Spaces with instant navigation.
Caveat: Permission-dependent. Instant switching temporarily overrides the corresponding Mission Control hotkeys and restores them when disabled or on quit.

Details: Select real windows, fill open space, grid a selection, swap two windows or stage a placement; keep changes or restore the original arrangement.
Caveat: Fill, Grid and Swap act immediately; Place is staged. Restore returns frames and stacking to the opening state. Requires window-control permissions.

Details: Open a searchable palette for project/session, group, layer, tiling and application commands; bare lats shows status without attaching.
Caveat: tmux-specific actions require tmux; native window operations require the running app.

Details: Keep project pane configuration in .lattices.json and layer/group declarations in ~/.lattices/workspace.json, refreshed by the app.
Caveat: This provides declarative configuration; a dedicated reusable template catalog and Git-management interface were not found in the audited core.

Capability: Menu bar and workspace entry points
Details: Native menu opens Home, project initialization and launch, Settings, companion apps, and workspace surfaces.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Empty query offers window placement, project launch/attach/kill, layers, groups, assistant, Studio, activity, Focus Mode, Settings and project refresh.
Caveat: This is the current merged surface; older documentation calls it a separate command palette and lists commands absent from the current browse menu.

Details: Typed slash commands expose engine intents; recognized natural-language commands preview the action and placement before Enter executes. Questions can hand off to the workspace assistant.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Search merges windows, terminal/session metadata, screen text, projects and applications; selecting a window result focuses that window.
Caveat: Screen text depends on enabled indexing and permissions; terminal metadata support varies by terminal.

Details: Maximize, centered floating, halves, quadrants, vertical and horizontal thirds, sixths, fourth columns, eighths and edge quarters share one placement model.
Caveat: Keyboard, HUD and local voice phrase coverage expose subsets of the full executor vocabulary.

Details: Place into arbitrary column/row grids, inclusive rectangular cell spans, and numbered square-grid shorthand.
Caveat: Compact human form uses one-based cells; explicit grid wire form uses zero-based cells.

Details: Resolve normalized rectangles through the same executor as named positions and grid cells; respect the display visible frame.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Distribute visible windows, windows of the frontmost app type, or a selected/app-filtered group inside a region.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Place the frontmost window in a least-occupied grid cell, or grow a selected window to available space from the in-place tools.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Move one window or a selection to a named/next monitor while retaining each normalized frame; a single window may move and take a canonical placement.
Caveat: Accessibility permission is needed; movement outcomes distinguish successful, partial, blocked and unverified operations.

Capability: Focus and find a window across Spaces
Details: Resolve tagged tmux terminal windows or explicit window IDs, switch Space when needed, raise and focus, and flash a visual border.
Caveat: Resolution falls back through CG/AX/AppleScript and differs by permissions and terminal support.

Details: Ctrl+Left/Right and mapped gestures switch adjacent Spaces with a landing bezel and edge feedback. The keyboard path uses a Dock swipe under a screen-update freeze.
Caveat: Requires Accessibility; uses private macOS facilities with fallback. Source coverage is not a guarantee on every macOS release.

Details: Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right exposes the Space landscape for the current display.
Caveat: Source entry point confirmed; visual interaction not exercised in this audit.

Details: Hold a configured modifier while dragging to reveal targets and a live preview; release over a zone to place. JSON rules set trigger rectangles, placements, priority and opacity.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Control+Option hold opens a radial ring or matrix around the cursor; aim at a target and release to place, or release at center to cancel.
Caveat: Shares the Control+Option hold with Spatial Lens through an exclusive preference mode.

Details: Preview and place the window under the pointer using eight surrounding targets; side placements cycle half/third/two-thirds, with deliberate adjacent-display flicks.
Caveat: Preference-selected alternative for the Control+Option hold; no live gesture test performed.

Details: Separate per-display window survey with selection, zoom, grouping, grid gather, staged placements and saving selected windows as layers.
Caveat: Staged Space reassignment is explicitly Phase 3 in source and must not be advertised as implemented.

Details: Select real desktop windows; Fill, Grid and Swap act immediately; Place stages an exact position. Keep accepts changes; Restore reverses the session frames and stacking.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Spotlight the frontmost interactive window against a dark backdrop, center/resize it, and restore its original frame on exit.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Capability: Letter navigation hints and mouse finder
Details: Overlay letter hints on windows for keyboard focus jumps; find or summon the pointer through engine commands.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Turn selected live windows into a tab stack; select, add, detach, expand to a grid, collapse, activate, show a guide or dissolve the group.
Caveat: These are runtime-only window stacks, distinct from persisted tmux project tab groups.

Details: Survey displays/layers; select and search windows; drag/resize, tile, spread, expose, distribute, grow, consolidate or flatten; preview, apply or discard edits.
Caveat: Some Screen Map implementation labels predate unified layer semantics. Current Overview dirty changes are being inventoried separately; do not equate screen-map local arrangements with saved layer rules.

Details: Search and inspect projects/windows, multi-select for tiling, display window previews and a docked/expanded minimap, and expose voice feedback.
Caveat: Pinning here pins the HUD inspector selection; it does not implement always-on-top for arbitrary application windows.

Capability: App-owned overlay actors and hover HUDs
Details: Apps can publish local HUD manifests and HTML; Lattices hosts a persistent actor with a transparent WebKit hover dashboard and global visibility toggle.
Caveat: Host capability requires an app-published manifest/content; the dashboard renderer and data remain app-owned.

Details: Map configured mouse buttons, clicks, directional drags and shapes to Space navigation, Screen Map, voice hotkey, arbitrary keyboard shortcuts or app activation; supports action sequences.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Load user-level gesture JSON, upsert/reload through the daemon, restore defaults and undo using local history snapshots.
Caveat: Machine-local rules are separate from project configuration; source docs specify newest 40 snapshots.

Details: Hold Caps Lock for Hyper and tap alone for Escape; preserve/restore the original HID mapping and provide stuck-input recovery.
Caveat: Optional and permission-dependent; uses private F18 transport to avoid latching Caps Lock.

Details: Record, change, disable and reset action bindings; detect conflicts; bind window, workspace, voice, HUD, layer and arrangement actions.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Event Viewer shows mouse/device observations; event-tap circuit breakers expose paused/disabled state and a re-enable control.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: Quick scans extract Accessibility text without screenshots; deep scans capture/hash windows and run budgeted Vision recognition, caching unchanged results.
Caveat: Opt-in. Default quick scan is 5 windows/60 seconds; deep scan 15 windows/2 hours with an OCR budget of 3. Screenshot OCR needs Screen Recording.

Details: Persist screen text in local SQLite/FTS5, search by text/app, inspect window history and recent results, and prune old records.
Caveat: Retention is configurable, with a current 7-day default; docs/ocr.md still says 3 days.

Details: Capture a window, rectangular region or full display; save PNGs as run artifacts and optionally copy to clipboard. Display capture supports delayed snapshot flows.
Caveat: Requires Screen Recording. Capture implementation exists, but no new media was captured during this inventory.

Capability: Artifact crop, zoom and local visual checks
Details: Crop/scale saved images, extract text blocks, verify contains/not-contains expectations, or compare artifact changes.
Caveat: The native vision analysis here is local OCR and image-change checking, not general semantic image reasoning by a vision language model.

Details: Record a screen region or application window to MOV through a signed app-host ScreenCaptureKit probe; choose region FPS/scale and stop the recording by run.
Caveat: Requires supported macOS, Screen Recording and an app bundle. Default window recording is a fixed region; explicit app-window mode follows the app-window path.

Details: Keep run status, target surfaces, trace events and media artifacts; inspect completed or failed activity through the app and API.
Caveat: Source-inspected; no live acceptance test in this audit.

Details: The action runtime supports dry-run placement/movement, target and before/after frame evidence, verification, receipt history and restoration of undoable actions.
Caveat: Undo and frame verification apply to the action-runtime path; do not assume every legacy/direct UI action has a durable receipt.

Details: Open directly into listening, hold Option for push-to-talk, stop/cancel capture, show transcript/intent/results, execute supported workspace intents and hand conversational questions to the assistant.
Caveat: Voice runtime is build-gated; SettingsView.swift:2235-2251 explicitly reports Not in this build when HUDSONKIT_WITH_VOICE is absent. Permissions and configured engines also apply.

Details: Voice turns use desktop snapshots, local/inference-backed interpretation and native action execution; preserve frame history, cap action batches and distribute repeated placement requests.
Caveat: Requires voice/worker readiness and any selected provider credentials. No latency or live provider-acceptance claim is established by this source audit.

Details: The Lattices voice API forwards say/stop/pause/resume/seek/skip, voice selection and speaker leases to the separately installed Voice helper.
Caveat: Speech has an independent lifecycle and capability token. A queued speech job is not proof of playback completion; voice.stop means output stop, not stopListening.

Capability: Settings, permissions and supported external terminals
Details: Settings cover app/project preferences, permissions, keyboard/mouse input, shortcuts, Hyperspace, voice/AI, screen search, companion pairing and Command Deck; launch tmux sessions in Terminal, iTerm2, Warp, Ghostty, Kitty or Alacritty.
Caveat: No native embedded-terminal UI was found. LatticesTerminalKit is a reusable terminal-inventory package, not an embedded terminal emulator. Companion and assistant details are audited separately.

Details: JSON request/response over WebSocket at 127.0.0.1:9399; real-time events; api.schema publishes methods, models, parameters and access levels. Source registers 130 literal methods plus 10 Voice helper schema methods (140 unique names).
Caveat: 140 is a count of current source registrations, not a live installed-app measurement; aliases are included. Older docs say 35+ or about 120.

Capability: TypeScript SDK and persistent project twin
Details: Package exports daemon client, assistant planner, CUA SDK and project-twin surface; ProjectTwin supports a persistent Pi process with invocation context, protocol, memory, events, model and effort options, plus optional OpenScout relay context.
Caveat: Daemon client is implemented; ProjectTwin requires the external Pi runtime. Do not present a project twin as an always-running native app service.

Details: Read windows and desktop snapshot, search indexed/live sources, list tmux sessions and inventory, projects, Spaces, layers, processes and process trees; synthesize terminal identities and capture exact terminal text; read OCR snapshots, search, history and recent scans.
Caveat: AX/OCR and terminal capture are distinct sources. This audit did not run scans or inspect live client data.

Capability: Target resolution, action receipts and undo
Details: Resolve window targets, execute typed actions with dry-run planning, inspect action history and undo recorded placements or batches. Receipts explain targets, plans, verification and trace.
Caveat: Undo is available for eligible recorded placement operations; it is not a general reversal of all computer-use input.

Details: Create/list/read runs and artifacts; save window, region or display screenshots; zoom an existing artifact.
Caveat: Screen capture requires macOS permission. Artifacts are run evidence; generation is not visual review.

Details: Record a window or region to a movie and stop recording; CLI can record a target while executing an action command.
Caveat: A start acknowledgement is not completed video verification. Lattices capture overlaps with the separate Action product.

Details: Snapshot a target window as AX, screenshot or both; expose element IDs and tree metadata; press, show menu, focus, type into an element, and set its value.
Caveat: Element references are snapshot-local. Background-safe operations depend on the requested AX action and target app.

Details: Target a window, session or app; send keys/hotkeys, click/double-click/right-click, scroll or drag, then request verification. Operations expose stage, present and execute treatments.
Caveat: Availability depends on macOS permissions and target behavior; default staging is not proof that a mutation executed.

Details: Prepare a terminal target, focus a verified window, launch a Mac app, type into ordinary app windows or safe terminal targets, and run terminal/Scout demonstration helpers.
Caveat: Demo helpers are specialist execution workflows, not general workspace navigation.

Details: Show a recorded cursor or magic cursor with app-owned appearance, motion and captions; configure cursor appearance; find or summon the real mouse.
Caveat: Synthetic presentation and real pointer input are separate operations.

Capability: Local image text analysis and native browser reads
Details: Analyze a captured window or saved image with local Vision OCR; extract text and evaluate contains/not-contains expectations. Native browser RPC exposes text, DOM query and JavaScript methods.
Caveat: Native image analysis is local text recognition and explicit checks, not provider-backed semantic image understanding. Native browser RPC is distinct from browser MCP and depends on browser support.

Details: Publish and clear screen-local toasts, labels, highlights and pet layers, with target display, lifetime, style, opacity and ordering.
Caveat: These are overlay canvas layers, separate from persistent workspace layers.

Capability: Persistent actors and project web HUDs
Details: Publish clickable app/sprite actors, animate them, attach URL/HTML hover HUDs and toggle the actor layer; CLI registers, discovers, publishes and synchronizes project HUD manifests.
Caveat: Actor renderer currently supports sprites. A hover web HUD is not a native app integration by itself.

Details: lats mcp serves stdio JSON-RPC with lazy toolset selection and harness config output. Current registry contains one toolset, browser, with 14 tools.
Caveat: Do not label the whole native daemon API as available through MCP. Native workspace methods currently use CLI/daemon/SDK.

Details: List, select and inspect named Action-owned Chrome profiles; unknown identity names create a blank profile on first open; report optional companion extension health.
Caveat: These are separate browser identities, not the user's regular Chrome profiles.

Details: Import selected cookies from a chosen regular Chrome profile into an isolated browser identity with a domain allowlist and dry-run default.
Caveat: Writing cookies requires explicit confirmation within the tool contract and appropriate authorization; no blanket signed-in assumption.

Details: Open URLs in the controlled isolated Chrome or hand a URL to regular Chrome; list/open tabs and enforce a navigation readiness deadline.
Caveat: Regular Chrome mode is an open-only handoff, not DOM-controlled access to everyday browser tabs.

Details: Read page metadata, visible text and selectors for interactive elements; inspect console calls, uncaught errors, promise rejections and Chrome resource/CSP logs.
Caveat: Complete console coverage applies to tabs opened through browser_open; tool responses report coverage.

Details: Click by CSS selector or visible text, fill form/contenteditable controls and wait for paint, navigation, network idle, selector appearance or disappearance.
Caveat: These actions operate only on the active isolated browser identity.

Details: Set exact per-tab emulated viewport or resize the hosting window; choose device pixel ratio, mobile emulation and media-query assertions; reset overrides.
Caveat: Per-tab overrides are reversible and session-local; physical window size can be clamped by the display.

Details: Capture PNGs of viewport, one selected element, an explicit document rectangle, or the full page; save locally and optionally return pixels.
Caveat: Full-page capture has a Chrome maximum-edge limit and reports truncation.

Details: Close an owned tab or release the session browser; browser quits only once no other live session claims it. MCP toolsets own initialization and idle bookkeeping.
Caveat: No lifecycle call closes the user's regular Chrome.

Details: The menu bar process hosts Hudson Voice/Vox live transcription at port 9398; command window uses push-to-talk; transcript routes to local intent matching and optional provider interpretation.
Caveat: Requires a voice-enabled build (HUDSONKIT_WITH_VOICE), permissions and configured engines. Input is app-owned and stops with Lattices; synthesis uses the separate Voice helper.

Details: List and execute intents, simulate spoken text, preview the TypeScript assistant plan, and invoke hands-off command interpretation. Voice targets the same window/layer/optimization executor as scripted actions.
Caveat: Provider-backed interpretations require a configured runtime or credentials; local command coverage is broader evidence than any specific natural-language example.

Details: Workspace chat first uses local agent-runtime/ACP harness, then a saved HudsonAI provider key, then a Scout project session. Picker supports Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode; model choices are supported for Claude/Codex/Pi and reasoning effort for Codex.
Caveat: Current source contradicts older Scout-only assistant documentation. Each route requires its corresponding installed/authenticated service; OpenCode adapter currently ignores model selection.

Details: Lattices forwards voice.say/stop/pause/resume/skip/seek/list/select/lease/release to separately installed Voice. The helper owns synthesis, queue, playback, HUD, preferences and authenticated RPC; leases prevent overlapping agents.
Caveat: Requires installed and running Voice plus capability authorization. The reply to say means queued, not playback completed. Legacy internal identifiers remain speech.*.

Capability: System, cloud and local synthesis providers
Details: Voice catalog includes macOS system voices, OpenAI, ElevenLabs and Kokoro; provider voice availability is queried rather than invented; Kokoro uses an in-process Neural Engine runtime.
Caveat: Cloud providers need credentials; Kokoro needs compiled support and a ready model. Source support was inspected, no live synthesis was run.

Details: Lattices Apps catalog presents Blink, Action and Voice as separate standalone products, with Install when missing and Open when installed. lats action provides status, install, launch and raw agent calls.
Caveat: They have independent app lifecycles and releases. Catalog registration does not establish current downloaded artifact availability.

Details: Mac host publishes manifest, snapshot and perform contract; deck controls voice, app/window switching, layer activation, optimize, frontmost placement/resize, focus, undo and optional Talkie actions.
Caveat: Talkie controls depend on Talkie. Deck is a thin control surface over Mac execution, not a second desktop engine.

Details: Bonjour discovery on port 5287, explicit Mac approval, per-device agreement, signed timestamp/nonce requests, encrypted payloads and per-route capability grants.
Caveat: Bridge is disabled by default. Source presence does not prove App Store distribution or connectivity to any particular device.

Capability: iPhone/iPad host roster and fleet controls
Details: Lattices Deck has a Home roster, one-Mac host view and multi-host fleet destination; tracks reachable/trusted machines, attention and activity, with per-host voice selection.
Caveat: Do not infer a cloud relay service from the Home cloud status UI; this is current iOS source, not a device validation.

Capability: Trackpad, key chords and clipboard transfer
Details: Send trackpad events, key chords and phone text to the paired Mac; switch Spaces and focus displays; find/summon mouse. Phone paste restores the Mac clipboard.
Caveat: Control is scoped by pairing capabilities; synthesized Space hotkeys route through Mac space switching.

Details: Display a paired Mac screenshot, select a display, manually refresh or auto-refresh one JPEG at a time, pausing/resuming updates.
Caveat: This is a read-only preview with a two-second refresh interval, not a high-frame-rate remote desktop stream.

Details: Start, stop, cancel and prewarm voice on the selected Mac, with phase, transcript and error state reflected back in deck snapshots.
Caveat: The iPad does not capture microphone audio; voice commands use the selected Mac microphone.

Capability: Native automation, capture and artifact review
Details: Separate signed Action.app with its own local agent, permissions, WebKit, screenshot and ScreenCaptureKit recording, guided capture, replay/review, session traces, AX/OCR observations, target resolution and deterministic act.execute.
Caveat: Implemented action kinds are click, type, press-key, drag, scroll, focus-window and open-app. Recording completion requires finished marker/status. Full trace-to-scenario generation and production composition remain roadmap.

Capability: Supervised drive leases and presentation stage
Details: Name the automation driver/task, begin/release/status a drive lease, publish short status notes, aim a synthetic cursor, play note/aim/wait/act beats, and set/clear/status a scene drape.
Caveat: Background drive is supported; attention approval is explicitly not available yet. This source includes ongoing dirty supervision/coordinate work and has not been live-verified in this audit.

Capability: Spatial Markdown notes with agent file interface
Details: One floating panel per note; capture, place, recall, edit/read, shade and restore geometry. Markdown with frontmatter is durable truth; CLI list/cat/new/present/type/write/search/log, named brandable workspaces, and desk open/move/focus/close/screens all converge through NoteStore.
Caveat: Blink owns note/panel lifecycle independently. Proposed agent HTTP/API documents and proposed live-plane collision/scene behavior are not implemented claims.

Details: iPhone/iPad receives complete note snapshots over encrypted LAN with explicit Mac approval, offline cache, identity binding and revocable device trust.
Caveat: Read-only; LAN is the implemented route. Tailscale/hosted-relay paths are future providers, not fallback capabilities.

Details: CLI detects project type, starts dev command, builds, restarts, reports logs and daemon health, updates CLI/app, launches/quits/rebuilds native app; root scripts expose type checks, app build, CLI/e2e tests and product-family checks.
Caveat: Source toolchain capability, not confirmation that all builds/tests pass or releases are current.

Details: Repository contains product skills for lattices, action, voice and blink; agent docs provide method discovery, exact terminal capture, canonical action/placement contracts, dry runs, receipts and docs artifacts.
Caveat: Some docs retain stale lats/speech skill labels, obsolete standalone Action Browser plugin wording, or describe the speaking helper as embedded. Current source, product AGENTS contracts and MCP registry are authoritative.
